section_summary: This section consists chiefly of 1948 correspondence between the State Department and holders or agents of defaulted Japanese dollar bonds. The Department records holdings, directs investors toward the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and says that settlement and peace treaty provisions remain uncertain. Other papers concern mortgages on Japanese utility bonds, claims against vested assets, an Irish diplomatic inquiry, and a request to trace securities taken to Argentina.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to a Japanese bondholder
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains its position on Japanese dollar bonds and requests details of the holder's bonds and citizenship.
subfiles.summary: The Department describes the Protective Council's role, its transmission of bond information to Tokyo, uncertainty over the peace treaty, and information needed to record a claim.

subfiles.title: Bondholder's reply to Corliss
subfiles.from: Unclear correspondent
subfiles.about: The writer acknowledges Corliss's May 17 letter concerning registration of Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Brief, heavily degraded reply about recording Japanese bond holdings.

subfiles.title: Reply to Mrs. Blyth about a Tokyo bond
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department answers Blyth's earlier inquiry about a $1,000 Tokyo bond.
subfiles.summary: It records her information, explains that it does not negotiate directly for holders, suggests contacting the Protective Council, and notes uncertainty over future settlement.

subfiles.title: Reply to Dr. Hess about Nippon Electric Power bonds
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department addresses Hess's inquiry into Nippon Electric Power dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: It suggests contacting the company in Japan, explains the Department's policy and the Protective Council's role, and lists bond and citizenship details needed for its records.

subfiles.title: Reply to Frank Y. Toribara about Japanese bonds
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department responds to Toribara's inquiry about Japanese bonds purchased through American banks.
subfiles.summary: It explains its limited role, recommends the Protective Council, and invites bond and citizenship information while treaty arrangements remain unknown.

subfiles.title: Charge slip for Friedman correspondence
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: A file charge slip tracks the Friedman bondholder correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Administrative charge slip for the Friedman file.

subfiles.title: Request for details from Augusta Friedman
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department seeks more information about Friedman's German and Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Corliss requests identifying, purchase, interest, and citizenship details before answering her inquiry.

subfiles.title: Reply to Hess about vested Nippon Electric Power assets
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains how vesting Nippon Electric Power assets affects Hess's position as a claimant.
subfiles.summary: A claim against vested assets would make Hess a debt claimant to those assets; treaty treatment remains unknown.

subfiles.title: Hess inquiry about Nippon Electric Power vesting
subfiles.from: C. L. Hess
subfiles.about: Hess asks whether vesting company assets changes his position as a bond claimant.
subfiles.summary: He cites advice from United States Attorney John C. Lehr about filing an alien property claim.

subfiles.title: Colucci request for help collecting coupons
subfiles.from: Frank Colucci
subfiles.about: Colucci seeks advice on collecting Japanese bond interest coupons.
subfiles.summary: He asks how to secure payment and requests return of his enclosure.

subfiles.title: Colucci letter to the Office of Alien Property
subfiles.from: Frank Colucci
subfiles.about: Colucci describes a $1,000 Shinyetsu Electric Power bond whose coupons have gone unpaid since 1941.
subfiles.summary: He identifies the bond and fiscal agent and asks how to obtain overdue and future coupon payments.

subfiles.title: Reply to Colucci about Shinyetsu Electric Power bond
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department responds to Colucci's Shinyetsu Electric Power bond inquiry.
subfiles.summary: It explains its bondholder policy, points to the Protective Council, and requests citizenship information for its record.

subfiles.title: Colgrove citizenship statement
subfiles.from: L. E. Colgrove
subfiles.about: Colgrove supplies citizenship information concerning his Imperial Japanese Government bonds.
subfiles.summary: He states that he is an American citizen by birth and will contact the Protective Council.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Colgrove
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges Colgrove's additional bond information.
subfiles.summary: It will record the submitted data for possible future use.

subfiles.title: Reply to Sumajiro Harada about Tokyo Electric Light bonds
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department responds to Harada's inquiry about Tokyo Electric Light dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: It outlines its policy, recommends the Protective Council, and seeks full bond and citizenship details for its records.

subfiles.title: Reply to Dillon, Read & Company about foreign bond issues
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department discusses Japanese, German, Italian, and Polish bonds in whose offerings the firm participated.
subfiles.summary: Corliss describes the Protective Council's role and a request to reinstate Japanese utility mortgages. He says no listed power plants are known to have been removed as reparations, explains the uncertain position of German issues, and points to developments concerning Italian and Polish payments.

subfiles.title: Hamilton submission of Shafer bond claim
subfiles.from: Robert Dow Hamilton
subfiles.about: Hamilton submits his client's claim concerning Japanese government and government-guaranteed bonds.
subfiles.summary: He describes $16,000 in Imperial Japanese Government bonds and $44,000 in Oriental Development Company bonds.

subfiles.title: Copy of alien property debt claim
subfiles.from: R. M. Shafer
subfiles.about: A duplicate claim form accompanies Hamilton's letter about Shafer's Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: The form records a debt claim based on Japanese government and Oriental Development Company securities.

subfiles.title: Reply to Hamilton about Shafer's bonds
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department answers Hamilton's inquiry on Shafer's Japanese bond holdings.
subfiles.summary: It explains the Protective Council's role, uncertainty over a treaty settlement, and additional purchase and citizenship facts needed for its records.

subfiles.title: Irish inquiry about Japanese bondholders
subfiles.from: Minister of Ireland
subfiles.about: The Irish minister asks whether Irish holders, including Athlone Woollen Mills, can recover on Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: The note specifically mentions Japanese 5½% conversion loan bonds of 1930.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to the Irish minister
subfiles.from: Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department addresses possible treatment of Irish-owned Japanese government dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: It cannot predict treaty terms but describes the American Protective Council's general policy of seeking benefits for holders regardless of nationality. Subject to possible special procedures, it knows of no reason a qualifying prewar Irish holder should receive different treatment from an American holder.

subfiles.title: Reply to Kellogg about Japanese and German bonds
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department replies about Imperial Japanese Government bonds and insufficiently identified German bonds.
subfiles.summary: It requests details of the German issues, explains its policy on Japanese government bonds, and asks for citizenship information before recording Kellogg's holdings.

subfiles.title: File charge record
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: An administrative form tracks a bondholder file.
subfiles.summary: Mostly blank file charge record.

subfiles.title: Graham statement of bond ownership
subfiles.from: Douglas Graham
subfiles.about: Graham supplies requested details about five Great Consolidated Electric Power bonds.
subfiles.summary: He gives serial numbers, purchase circumstances, the last interest payment, and his American citizenship by birth.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Douglas Graham
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges Graham's additional information about five utility bonds.
subfiles.summary: It will record the information for possible future consideration.

subfiles.title: Reply to Dillon, Read & Company on utility mortgages
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department addresses the firm's request to restore mortgages securing Japanese utility bonds.
subfiles.summary: It is studying the issue and has asked the Reparations and Restitution Delegation for its views.

subfiles.title: Reply to Stewart C. Pratt on Ujigawa mortgage
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department answers Pratt's request to reconstitute the mortgage securing Ujigawa Electric Power bonds.
subfiles.summary: It reports ongoing study and its request for the Reparations and Restitution Delegation's views.

subfiles.title: Reply to John F. Sherin
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department discusses Sherin's City of Yokohama and German corporate bonds.
subfiles.summary: It distinguishes the government-linked Yokohama bonds from the private German issue, describes the Protective Council's role, and requests holding and citizenship details. It also points him to the Office of Alien Property for information on claims against vested assets.

subfiles.title: Sherin inquiry about Japanese and German bonds
subfiles.from: John F. Sherin
subfiles.about: Sherin asks for advice on three City of Yokohama bonds and two German steel company bonds.
subfiles.summary: He identifies five $1,000 bonds and requests information.

subfiles.title: Hamilton supplies Shafer bond details
subfiles.from: Robert Dow Hamilton
subfiles.about: Hamilton supplies serial numbers and further ownership information for Shafer's bonds.
subfiles.summary: He lists Japanese government and Oriental Development Company bond numbers and says Shafer is American by birth.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Hamilton
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges additional information on Shafer's bonds.
subfiles.summary: It will place Hamilton's information in its records.

subfiles.title: Request for Hamilton correspondence
subfiles.from: A. Waskam
subfiles.about: A file request seeks Robert Dow Hamilton correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Administrative request for Hamilton's July letter.

subfiles.title: Charge slip for Hamilton correspondence
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: A charge slip tracks a letter to Robert Dow Hamilton.
subfiles.summary: Administrative charge slip for Hamilton correspondence.

subfiles.title: Request to trace bonds taken to Buenos Aires
subfiles.from: David L. Bazelon, Office of Alien Property
subfiles.to: George W. Baker, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Office of Alien Property seeks help locating securities taken from a Japanese firm's New York branch to Buenos Aires.
subfiles.summary: Bazelon asks State Department representatives to determine whether Y. Takeuchi still controls a Buenos Aires safe deposit box and the American and Argentine bonds reportedly placed there.

subfiles.title: O'Callahan inquiry about a Yokohama bond
subfiles.from: Norma O'Callahan
subfiles.about: O'Callahan asks for information about her City of Yokohama 6% bond.
subfiles.summary: She says the Office of Alien Property suggested contacting the Department.

subfiles.title: Reply to Norma O'Callahan
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department answers O'Callahan's inquiry about her Yokohama bond.
subfiles.summary: It explains its policy, suggests the Protective Council, and requests acquisition, interest, and citizenship information for its records.

subfiles.title: Farrell claim on Caughey's Ujigawa bond
subfiles.from: J. Paul Farrell
subfiles.about: Farrell files notice of Frances Grace Caughey's Ujigawa Electric Power bond.
subfiles.summary: He identifies the $1,000 bond and offers to complete a prescribed claim form if needed.

subfiles.title: Reply to Farrell about Caughey's bond
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains available steps concerning Caughey's Ujigawa Electric Power bond.
subfiles.summary: It describes the Protective Council's mortgage reinstatement request, uncertainty over treaty treatment, and details needed to record Caughey's claim. It also mentions debt claims against vested Japanese assets.

subfiles.title: O'Callahan supplies acquisition and citizenship details
subfiles.from: Norma O'Callahan
subfiles.about: O'Callahan supplements the record of her City of Yokohama bond.
subfiles.summary: She gives family purchase and inheritance dates, purchase price, last interest payment, and naturalization details.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to O'Callahan
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department responds to O'Callahan's supplemental letter.
subfiles.summary: A brief, poorly reproduced acknowledgment of her September information.

subfiles.title: Crawford account of an inherited Japanese bond
subfiles.from: Mrs. N. Earle Crawford
subfiles.about: Crawford explains how an Oriental Development Company bond came into her possession.
subfiles.summary: She says her mother-in-law gave the bond to her husband, who has since died, and describes her joint ownership and citizenship by birth. She encloses correspondence and money to cover registered return of the papers.

subfiles.title: Receipt for Crawford enclosures
subfiles.from: Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department records valuable enclosures received with Crawford's letter.
subfiles.summary: Receipt notes a Japanese bond, letters, and one dollar.

subfiles.title: National City Bank explanation to Crawford
subfiles.from: Nelson Stuart, National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: The bank explains the status of Crawford's Oriental Development Company debenture and unpaid coupons.
subfiles.summary: It describes denied licensing for a 1941 coupon, later defaults, claims filed against vested assets, and the option of an individual claim. It lists known vesting orders and recommends registering the holding with the State Department and Protective Council.

subfiles.title: Dubbs family letter about the Oriental Development bond
subfiles.from: Bill Dubbs
subfiles.to: Family of Mrs. N. Earle Crawford
subfiles.about: Dubbs reports inquiries he made in Tokyo about the family's Oriental Development Company bond.
subfiles.summary: Bank and Civil Property Custodian staff advised contacting the National City Bank in New York.

subfiles.title: Reply to Crawford and return of enclosures
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges Crawford's bond information and returns her enclosures.
subfiles.summary: It records her information, refers to the bank's account, and returns the letters, bond, and dollar bill.

subfiles.title: D'Amico inquiry on Nelson's utility bond
subfiles.from: Daniel I. D'Amico
subfiles.about: D'Amico asks how Mrs. Conrad Nelson can protect her Great Consolidated Electric Power bond after missing a claim deadline.
subfiles.summary: He says Nelson believed earlier registration of the bond protected her rights.

subfiles.title: Office of Alien Property reply to D'Amico
subfiles.from: David L. Bazelon, Office of Alien Property
subfiles.about: The Office of Alien Property advises D'Amico that the debt-claim filing period has expired.
subfiles.summary: It gives the August 8, 1948 deadline and refers him to the State Department.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to D'Amico about Nelson's bond
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains its position on Nelson's Japanese government-guaranteed utility bond.
subfiles.summary: It distinguishes private issuers from government-guaranteed obligations, suggests contacting the Protective Council, and says treaty treatment remains uncertain. It offers to record Nelson's holding if her American citizenship is documented.
